idiom_name: driver.Valuer + sql.Scanner over a jsonb/TEXT column (encoding/json)
implementation_notes: database/sql already defines the two hooks a serialized column needs and the entity implements them: Value() (driver.Valuer) returns json.Marshal(e) as []byte for the jsonb/TEXT column, and Scan(src) (sql.Scanner) reverses it, so the type flows through any driver without an ORM. The struct tags double as the payload schema, which is why the local idiom replaces the classic serializer class. When GORM is already the data layer the hook exists as a tag - gorm:"serializer:json" - and neither method is needed; write the Valuer/Scanner pair yourself when you use database/sql directly or when the codec should stay explicit.
pitfalls: Scan receives nil for SQL NULL (and some drivers hand back string rather than []byte): an unchecked type assertion panics on real data.
json.Marshal writes exported fields only, so unexported state silently disappears from the payload.
Cyclic values make Marshal loop forever, and decoding into interface{} loses the concrete Go types unless you use json.Number or a typed payload.
Scan must mutate through a pointer receiver - a value-receiver Scan cannot store the decoded entity.
